page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual server driven by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The configuration provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with two threads per core. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD, and the platform includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark measurements indicate pronounced single-core capabilities contrasted with average multi-threaded scaling. In stress-ng single-core testing, the instance achieved a top-tier score of 3394.17, supported by a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2125.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.64 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory write throughput also reached the top quartile at 106.77 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the 4-vCPU hardware ceiling, yielding average results in stress-ng multi-core (13418.26), Geekbench multi-core (6739.0), and Clang software compilation. PassMark database operations and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranked in the lower quartile.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation positions this server for compute-centric rather than memory-intensive tasks. The absence of a discrete GPU and the 8.0 GB RAM constraint prevent viable deployment of medium-to-large language models, with 7B LLM inference exhibiting low throughput. However, the dedicated core architecture and high-speed local NVMe make it efficient for predictable execution profiles. Suitable workloads include continuous integration workers, code compilation, text and batch processing pipelines, and lightweight application services that rely on fast single-thread performance.
